name: Ulch
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Sunik, O. P. 1985. Ul'chskij jazyk: issledovanija i materialy. Leningrad: Nauka.

new_statements.quote: Ударение в ульчском языке, как и в нанайском или удэгейском языках, является экспираторно-музыкальным: на гласный первого слога падает слабое экспираторное ударение, на гласный последнего слога — тоническое (или музыкальное). Гласный первого слога артикулируется наиболее отчетливо. Гласный последнего слога, напротив, артикулируется нечетко, но с некоторым, иногда малозаметным, повышением тона. Именно в последнем слоге слова происходят поэтому чаще всего фонетические процессы редукции, нейтрализации фонологических противопоставлений некоторых гласных или их усечение.
new_statements.translation: Stress in the Ulch language, as in Nanai or Udihe, is expiratory-musical: a weak expiratory stress falls on the vowel of the first syllable, and a tonic (or musical) accent on the vowel of the last syllable. The vowel of the first syllable is articulated most distinctly. The vowel of the last syllable, on the contrary, is articulated indistinctly, but with a certain, sometimes barely noticeable, rise in pitch. It is therefore in the last syllable of the word that phonetic processes of reduction, neutralization of the phonological oppositions of certain vowels, or their truncation most often take place.
new_statements.citation: Sunik, O. P. 1968. Ульчский язык. In: Языки народов СССР, т. 5: Монгольские, тунгусо-маньчжурские и палеоазиатские языки. Ленинград: Наука, pp. 149–171.
new_statements.locator: § 4 (Фонетика), p. 152, last paragraph; supporting sentence § 2, p. 150
new_statements.rule_in_words: Two-component accent of the Soviet 'expiratory-musical' type: the dynamic (expiratory) stress is fixed on the first syllable of the word, while the final syllable carries a pitch rise (tonic/musical accent) and is the site of vowel reduction and truncation. Read as fixed-initial for the dynamic stress; the final-syllable component is pitch, not a second dynamic stress. Sunik also says (p. 150) that a phonetically 'long' (doubled) vowel is the sound on which expiratory stress falls (examples ӡе́сал'и 'relatives', а́н'ӡи 'right side', бо́кто 'dwarf-pine nut', ӡу́jурул'и 'sour', а́мдавӯ 'imitate', кэ́нӡувэ̄ 'make a boat', н'у́иктэ 'nettle'), all marked on the initial syllable; he denies that phonological vowel length is established.
new_statements.secondary_stress: No secondary dynamic stress stated. The final syllable carries the tonic/musical accent (slight pitch rise) but is described as the weakly articulated, reduced syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated as exceptions. Long/doubled vowels attract the expiratory stress and length is used to make a contrast salient (н'иктэ 'child' vs н'у́иктэ 'nettle'; элэ 'enough' vs э́элэ 'skirt hem'); monosyllables have facultative length (p. 150).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level description of isolated words (illustrative citation forms); no phrase-level or instrumental data. Applies to Ulch as a whole; Sunik states the language is dialectally homogeneous (p. 149). Statement is impressionistic (1968); Menges 1968 notes no experimental-phonetic work even for Nanai, and Gorbunova 2019 lists none for Ulch.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Ulch as a whole (Sunik: dialectally homogeneous), materials from Bulava, Mongol, Kol'chem, Dudi (Ul'chsky district, Khabarovsk Krai), collected 1948 and 1964 with I. P. Val'dju and A. L. Val'dju, plus Petrova 1936 — identical to Glottolog ulch1241 (ISO ulc). The earlier scan named Sunik 1985; the statement quoted here is from Sunik's earlier 1968 sketch in Jazyki narodov SSSR, the same author and analysis.

sources.note: §4 p. 152: Ulch stress, like Nanai and Udihe, is 'expiratory-musical' — a weak expiratory (dynamic) stress on the first-syllable vowel and a tonic/musical accent (slight, sometimes barely noticeable pitch rise) on the last-syllable vowel; first-syllable vowel is articulated most clearly, last-syllable vowel is reduced/neutralized/truncated. §2 p. 150: phonetically 'long' (doubled) vowels are the sound on which expiratory stress falls (examples marked on initial syllables); phonological vowel length judged not established. Archive.org Rosetta Project scan; its ABBYY text layer is Latin garbage…

sources.citation: Fuchs, W., I. A. Lopatin, K. H. Menges & D. Sinor. 1968. Tungusologie (Handbuch der Orientalistik I.5.3). Leiden: Brill. (Menges, 'Die tungusischen Sprachen')
sources.note: Comparative survey; accent statements for Ewenki, Lamut, Udihe and Nanai (Nanai per Avrorin: musical-expiratory accent always on the final syllable) but no separate Olča/Ulcha accent statement (grep of full scanned text; index lists Oltschen only pp. 13, 17, 27f.).

sources.citation: Горбунова, В. А. 2019. Ульчский язык: современное состояние и перспективы изучения. Языки и фольклор коренных народов Сибири 1(37): 103–110. DOI 10.25205/2312-6337-2019-1-103-110.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. State-of-research survey: confirms that Petrova 1936 and Sunik 1985 are the only systematic descriptions, that Sunik 1985 gives 'more detailed description of phonetic regularities and processes', and that no experimental-phonetic work on Ulch exists; cites Kazama 2002 (Ulcha oral literature 2), 2003, 2010.

sources.citation: Endangered Languages of Siberia project page 'Ульчский язык' (lingsib.iea.ras.ru/ru/languages/ulch.shtml) and its bibliography page.
sources.note: Gives inventory (8 vowels long/short, 18 consonants, vowel harmony) but nothing on stress; bibliography lists Sunik 1968 (pp. 149–171), Sunik 1985, Petrova, Schmidt 1923, Kormushin 2002 (Красная книга, pp. 207–211).
